title: Gracious Redeemer, Shake
description: Gracious Redeemer, Shake in Tonic Solfa to DIADEMATA, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 305.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Short Metre Double (6.6.8.6.6.6.8.6), and this page sets them to DIADEMATA; any other Short Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Gra-cious Re-deem-er, shake This slum-ber from my soul! Say to me now, "A-wake, a_-wake! And Christ shall make thee whole." Lay to thy might-y hand! A-larm me in this hour, And make me ful-ly un-der-stand The thun-der of thy power.

lines: And Christ shall make thee whole."
Give me on thee to call,
For ever standing on my guard,
When to the right or left I turn,
Thy voice still let me hear;
O may I hearken and obey,
And shun the paths of sin!
My help and refuge in distress,
Give me to trust in thee.
My horn, and rock, and buckler be,
But strength in thee I surely have,
Thou, Jesus, love me as thy own,
And love me to the end.

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to DIADEMATA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
